content.text:
The funder names come from the parents’ **own declaration fields**. They are not copied from another child. Both payment records have `UltimatePayerName: null` and `IsUltimatePayerDifferent: false`; that combination tells the resolver to select the immediate parent’s payer.

| Payment | Amount | Immediate parent | Parent’s own `PayerName` |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| 14765 | £116.20 | 10624 | Google |
| 15494 | £270,000 | 11542 | Direct Bullion |

The live upstream responses contain Google in parent 10624’s latest version, register 734. Parent 11542 contains Direct Bullion in its own versions for registers 761 and 758. The separate `childInterests` array contains siblings; it is not the source of these names. The local `/members/5091` response returns those same funder names.

During ingestion, [declaration_source.rs](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/src/lib/outbound/declaration_source.rs:179) selects the latest declaration version by register publication date, then register ID. It extracts payer, donor and ultimate payer as separate observations. Its cleaning step retains a parent’s named payer even when that parent has no payment amount, so the parent remains available as evidence for its children.

The selection happens in [attribution.rs](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/src/lib/domain/models/declaration_resolution/attribution.rs:7):

- An explicitly named ultimate payer takes precedence.
- If the ultimate payer is marked different but unnamed, attribution is unavailable.
- If it is marked **not different**, select the immediate parent’s payer.
- If the flag is absent, try the payment’s own donor, then its own payer.

For these two entries, the third rule applies. [Parent selection](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/src/lib/domain/models/declaration_resolution/attribution.rs:75) requires exactly one usable payer observation on the immediate parent, belonging to the same member and extracted from that declaration’s own fields. It does not search siblings or grandparents. Missing, unusable or ambiguous parent evidence produces unavailable attribution. Name resolution subsequently determines how the selected observation is grouped; it does not invent the payer relationship. The HTTP API reads the stored result rather than recalculating it on each request.

The documented rationale is to preserve what Parliament actually reports while making the reporting-funder choice separately. [Issue #16](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/issues/16) explicitly asks to retain separate names and nulls to avoid inventing source information; [PR #23](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/23) describes preserving the roles and independently selecting the funder. The original design document explicitly accepts one-hop parent attribution based on the source descriptions, but that document is agent-authored evidence—not proof of an original human ruling about every possible parent or sibling case.

Confidence is high about these records and the current calculation. We cannot establish whether an older upstream snapshot omitted the parent names, or recover an undocumented human rationale for sibling handling.

Coverage: git history, relevant PRs, GitHub issues and repository design documents were examined. Drive searches for Exposed, payer, funder, Parliament, Nigel Farage and inheritance found no relevant documents. Team chat, infrastructure observability, exception tracking and analytics warehouse tools were unavailable.

My recommendation is to expose this provenance in the UI: “Google — payer recorded on parent declaration 10624,” with a parent link. That would make the supported attribution understandable without making it look as though Google was explicitly named on payment 14765.
